A comment explaining why grouping matters here.
The config validates and every existing ecosystem entry still works.
guidance: `.github/dependabot.yml` already covers nine ecosystems and ignores the pinned JS SDK — do not disturb those rules.
Each adapter has its own `go.mod`, which is why they are separate ecosystems today.
Keep the pinned-generator ignores exactly as they are; they protect the correctness gate.

title: chore: assert the CLI prints no secret on any error path
description: A test that runs every subcommand's error paths with a recognisable secret in the environment and asserts it appears in no output.
why: The rule that the CLI never prints a secret is stated in `main.go`'s package comment and enforced by review. A test makes it enforced by the build, and the error paths are where a value leaks into a message by accident.
criteria: Runs every subcommand with a distinctive seed in the environment and asserts it appears in neither stream.
Covers usage errors, decode errors and signing refusals, not just the success path.
Iterates the dispatcher's subcommands so a newly added one is covered automatically.
Fails loudly if it finds no subcommands, so it cannot pass vacuously.
guidance: `runCLIEnv` already injects a fake environment — use it rather than touching the real one.
Iterating the dispatcher is what makes this durable; a hand-written list will go stale.
Check the error value's text too, not only the streams, since `main` prints it.

title: chore: record the tool versions a CI run used
description: Print the resolved versions of Go, Node, Rust, stellar-cli and the pinned SDKs at the start of each CI job.
why: Several pins are floors rather than exact versions, and `check-latest` is set on the Go setup. When a job fails on a runner and passes locally, the first question is which versions ran, and the logs do not say.
criteria: Each job logs the versions relevant to it, early enough to be visible before a failure.
Covers the adapter modules' own toolchains, which may differ from the root's.
Also surfaced in the job summary, not only the log.
No secret or token is printed.
guidance: A Dependabot bump once took an adapter to a newer Go floor than the root — that is the case this makes diagnosable.
Keep it to a few lines per job; verbose output defeats the purpose.
The job summary is where a reviewer will actually look.

title: test: assert the golden vector set covers every credential arm
description: A test asserting at least one committed vector exists for each of the four credential arms.
why: `loadVectors` fails if the directory is empty, which catches total deletion. It does not catch the loss of every vector for one arm, and an arm with no vector is an arm with no byte-level proof.
criteria: Decodes each vector, classifies its arm, and fails naming any arm with no coverage.
Reports the per-arm count, so thinning is visible before it reaches zero.
Fails loudly on an empty vector set rather than passing vacuously.
Deleting one arm's vectors is demonstrated to fail the test, and not committed.
guidance: Classify by decoding, not by filename; a name is a convention and not evidence.
`golden_test.go` already has the loader and the empty-set guard — extend it.
The per-arm count in the output is what makes a slow erosion visible.

title: test: assert the sentinel errors are all distinct
description: A test asserting no two exported sentinel errors are the same value or carry the same message.
why: There are twenty-nine sentinels matched with `errors.Is`. Two that compare equal would make a caller's branch silently wrong, and the existing meta-test checks only that each is mentioned by a test, not that each is distinguishable.
criteria: Asserts pairwise inequality by value and by message.
Reads the sentinel list from `errors.go` rather than a hand-written copy.
Fails loudly if it finds no sentinels.
A deliberate duplicate is demonstrated to fail, and not committed.
guidance: `errors_meta_test.go` already parses `errors.go` with `go/ast` — reuse that, do not duplicate the parsing.
Identical messages on distinct values are also worth catching: they make a failure unreadable even when the branch is right.
Keep the failure output naming both sentinels.

title: test: assert the no-mutation rule for every entry-taking function
description: A test that passes the same entry to every exported function taking one and asserts its bytes are unchanged afterwards.
why: The rule is stated in CONTRIBUTING and each function has its own mutation test. A newly added function inherits neither, and the XDR types alias pointers and slices by default, so forgetting the deep copy is the easy mistake.
criteria: Enumerates exported functions taking an entry and runs each against a shared fixture.
Asserts the fixture's marshalled bytes are identical afterwards.
Fails naming any function not covered, rather than silently skipping it.
Fails loudly if it enumerates nothing.
guidance: Reflection or AST enumeration both work; AST matches how the other meta-tests here are built.
Functions needing extra arguments can be given a documented default — skipping them defeats the purpose.
A function that mutates its input is a bug to report, not to accommodate in the test.

title: test: assert every CLI subcommand accepts --json
description: A test asserting each subcommand accepts `--json` and emits parseable JSON on both success and failure.
why: `--json` is documented as the consistent contract across subcommands, and consistency is asserted per subcommand where someone remembered. A new subcommand can ship without it and nothing fails.
criteria: Iterates the dispatcher's subcommands rather than a hand-written list.
Asserts parseable JSON on success and on an induced error.
Subcommands for which `--json` is meaningless are excluded explicitly with a reason.
Fails loudly if it finds no subcommands.
guidance: `TestSpecsCoverTheUsageText` shows how to enumerate subcommands from the real source.
Error output must stay on stdout in JSON mode with stderr empty — that is the existing contract, so assert it.
Explicit exclusions, not silent ones.

title: test: assert the fuzz seed corpora are valid and non-empty
description: A test asserting each fuzz target's seed corpus exists, is non-empty, and parses as the Go corpus format.
why: Go reads seeds only from `testdata/fuzz/<TargetName>/`, and a misnamed directory or a malformed file is silently ignored. The fuzzer then starts from nothing and still reports success, which is indistinguishable from a working corpus.
criteria: Asserts a non-empty corpus directory for every fuzz target in the repository.
Asserts each seed file parses as `go test fuzz v1`.
Fails naming any target with no corpus, including one added later.
A deliberately misnamed directory is demonstrated to fail, and not committed.
guidance: Enumerate the targets from the source so a new one is covered automatically.
`cmd/gencorpus` writes the corpus — reuse its understanding of the format rather than reimplementing the parser.
`docs/fuzzing.md` lists the targets; verify that list is still accurate while you are here.
